title: Add TTL expiry to a cache without disturbing its existing behaviour
prompt: src/cache.py implements an LRU cache that is used widely across the codebase and has a substantial existing test suite that currently passes. Add optional time-to-live expiry: LruCache(capacity, ttl=None, clock=time.monotonic). When ttl is set, an entry older than ttl seconds must be treated as absent by get, __contains__ and __len__, and must not occupy capacity. When ttl is None the cache must behave exactly as it does today. Every existing behaviour - LRU eviction order, statistics, the peek method that does not affect recency, and clear() - must continue to work unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: LruCache(capacity) with no ttl behaves exactly as before.
With a ttl, an entry older than ttl is invisible to get, __contains__ and __len__.
Expired entries do not consume capacity: inserting past capacity evicts expired entries first.
Expiry is measured against the injected clock, never wall-clock time.
get on an expired entry counts as a miss in the statistics, not a hit.
peek still returns a value without promoting recency, and still respects expiry.
LRU eviction order, clear() and the existing statistics are unchanged.
